summary: Starting in 2010, Sibutramine was pulled from the market in the United States and nine other countries because of heart harm and neurotoxicity, which is damage to the brain or nervous system [3]. In addition, a small computer model—not tests on people—rated the drug with a low liver risk score of 33 and a high heart risk score of 74 [M]. Multiple research trials involving the drug were terminated early, with reasons including withdrawal of the medicine from the market, findings from nonclinical studies, and ethical concerns about leaving a control group without treatment [5][6][7].
